about.title: About the project
about.lead: A playground for playing all {{count}} Katamino challenges by hand and watching, step by step, how a combinatorial optimization algorithm solves them.

game.title: The game
game.body: Katamino is a pentomino puzzle: pieces made of 5 squares. In each challenge a set of pieces has to cover a 5-row board exactly, with no gaps and no overlaps. The board size (the "PENTA") is the number of pieces used — the bigger, the harder.

play.title: How to play
play.pick: Click a piece to pick it up and click the board to drop it.
play.rotate: Right-click or R rotates the piece in hand.
play.mirror: E, or dragging the piece, mirrors it.
play.progress: Completed challenges are saved in this browser and show up marked in the list.

solver.title: The solver
solver.body: On any challenge, "Watch the solver" shows the search happening on the board. The base is always the same — try, undo, try again — and you build the strategy by switching on criteria that change the order things are tried in or spot a dead end earlier. Run different combinations on the same challenge and compare steps and backtracks.

tech.title: How it was built
tech.body: React, TypeScript and Vite, with no server: everything runs in your browser, and the solver works in a Web Worker so the screen never freezes. Available in Portuguese and English.

base.name: Try, undo, try again
base.summary: Always on: the search everything else builds on.
base.details: Takes the next empty square, tries a piece there and moves on. When it gets stuck, it removes the last piece and tries the next option. On its own it finds a solution eventually, but it only notices a mistake when nothing fits anymore.

scarcePiecesFirst.name: Stiffest pieces first
scarcePiecesFirst.summary: Tries the pieces with the fewest orientations before the flexible ones.
scarcePiecesFirst.details: Pieces like I and X can only be placed in one or two ways; pieces like F and L in eight. Placing the stiff ones while the board is still open avoids discovering late that they no longer fit anywhere.

mostConstrainedCell.name: Hardest square first
mostConstrainedCell.summary: Fills the empty square with the fewest possible placements.
mostConstrainedCell.details: Instead of following reading order, it counts for every empty square how many placements could cover it, and works on the one with the fewest. A square with a single option is a forced move; one with none shows the dead end immediately.

deadRegions.name: Rule out impossible holes
deadRegions.summary: Backs off when an empty area’s size is not a multiple of 5.
deadRegions.details: Every piece covers exactly 5 squares. If a placement walls off an empty area of 3, 7 or 11 squares, no combination of pieces can fill it exactly — so that placement is undone right away instead of being explored.

strandedCells.name: No square left without a way out
strandedCells.summary: Backs off when some empty square can no longer be covered by any remaining piece.
strandedCells.details: After each placement it checks every empty square: is there still a remaining piece that fits over it? If one square has no candidate left, filling the rest is pointless, and the placement is undone.

strandedPieces.name: Every piece still fits
strandedPieces.summary: Backs off when a remaining piece no longer fits anywhere.
strandedPieces.details: After each placement it checks every piece not yet used: is there still room for it somewhere on the board? If one of them fits nowhere, the board can never be completed from here.
